Traupman 66, 402

vītamīnum, vītamīnī n.

noun, second declension

A modern lexical form. Plural vītamīna, vītamīnōrum n. pl., vitamins, using the neuter form. The international term was coined from “vita” and “amine”; it does not imply that all vitamins are amines. The ī in vīta and the adopted international -amīn- reading give our convention vītamīnum; these are reconstructed Neo-Latin reading quantities, not attested Classical measurements.

Other words

  • vitamina, vitaminae f.

    noun, first declension · also used · modern · M-O

    The feminine variant, also recorded by Morgan–Owens, without documented stem quantities.

Examples

  • vītamīna D et B12

    vitamins D and B12composed

  • Hic cibus multa vītamīna continet.

    This food contains many vitamins.composed

See also nutrition, vitaminic, multivitamin.
